correctness.rationale: Write each base-b^k digit as a k-column base-b block and index exponents from zero. The base-b^k palindrome reverses block order. Reversal of all k(m-1)+s significant base-b digits sends a high-column digit at (j,c), s<=c<k, into block m-2-j and column k+s-1-c; block symmetry gives the adjacent-block recurrence, propagating the zero top padding to every block. For low columns it maps (j,c) to (m-1-j,s-1-c), yielding individual short palindromes, and both implications reverse. Exactly ceil(m/2) blocks are independent; one has (b-1)b^floor((s-1)/2) choices, all others b^ceil(s/2), giving F. The geometric series and two subsequential limits follow algebraically; strict AM–GM excludes a fixed leading constant. Actual standalone checker replayed 134 finite length bins and 1148558 integers; computation is corroboration, not proof.

originality.rationale: The primary 2014 paper explicitly notices infinitude when one base is an integral power of the other, but excludes such pairs from its quantitative results. The new all-length if-and-only-if block theorem yields exact intersection counts, a rational generating function, a parity-dependent logarithmic growth exponent, and unequal normalized constants; none is implied merely by the known exhibited infinite family. The inspected secondary literature concerns variable-base constructions or separate one-base counting functions. No equivalent or stronger covering statement was found in targeted literature and semantic prior comparisons, subject to residual search incompleteness.
residual_risks: An unpublished, unindexed, or differently phrased digit-combinatorics result could state the same complete classification or count.
The precise full cutoff fluctuation function between base powers is not derived; two differing subsequences suffice for the stated non-convergence.
Independent expert validation has not been performed.

value.rationale: The initial simultaneous-palindrome study treats integral-power bases as an infinite but quantitatively undeveloped exceptional regime. The theorem naturally classifies the entire fixed dependent-power intersection across all bases, exponents and lengths, giving exact enumerations and an explicit rational generating function. Its sparse-growth exponent jumps according to parity of the exponent and its normalized count oscillates between distinct constants; these are mathematically useful quantitative baselines for comparisons with multiplicatively independent bases, and not merely a selected numerical slice or renaming of an obvious palindrome identity.
